fields.text: Item 9+ Magnetite Scope Magical Source Guns & Gears (Remastered) pg. 181 PFS Note Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons. Usage attached to firearm (scope) Bulk L More of a field projector than a scope, this small cylinder of magnetite has been enchanted to spread and accelerate the shrapnel of a scatter weapon further than the weapon's natural capabilities. Furthermore, some of the floating magnetite inside the scope's structure can help you when attempting to determine the your allies' locations. The magnetite scope grants you a +2 item bonus to Survival checks to Sense Direction when using the scope to assist you in navigating. This scope can only be attached to firearms with the scatter trait. Activate Single Action (manipulate) Effect The next Strike you make this round with the gun to which the scope is attached has its scatter radius increased by 5 feet. Item 9 Magnetite Scope Source Guns & Gears (Remastered) pg. 181 Price 800 gp Bulk L Item 17 Magnetite Scope (Greater) Source Guns & Gears (Remastered) pg. 181 Price 16,000 gp Bulk L The item bonus is +3, and activating the scope increases the scatter radius by 10 feet.

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 181

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Characters with access to firearms gain access to accessories that can be used with those weapons._

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** attached to firearm or crossbow (scope)

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

These scopes use magically enhanced lenses to extend the range of your weapon and help spot distant foes. The scope grants you a +1 item bonus to visual Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) creatures through the scope.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** While gazing through the scope, you zoom in on your targets to make it easier to hit them at a distance. You increase the [range increment](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) of the weapon to which the scope is attached by 5 feet until the beginning of your next turn or until you're no longer wielding the weapon, whichever comes first.

>
[Stampede Medallion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5189)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Eidolon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=386" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 245

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When crafted, a _stampede medallion_ looks like nothing more than small silver disk, about the same size as a silver piece. When you invest this medallion for your eidolon, it changes shape to appear as a tiny, bejeweled facsimile of the eidolon, magically attached just over your eidolon’s heart. While your eidolon wears the medallion, they gain a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382). 

**Activate—Impossible Tide** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your eidolon momentarily manifests into a stampede of dozens of copies of themself. The stampede rampages out in every direction, swerving around your allies while trampling any foe on the ground in an [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) around your eidolon with a radius equal to your eidolon’s Speed. Each of these foes takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage, with a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save. On a critical failure, the foe is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). After dealing damage, the stampede of eidolons vanishes as quickly as it appeared.

>
[Stormshard](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3742)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Triumph of the Tusk</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #208: Hoof, Cinder, and Storm](/Sources.aspx?ID=250) pg. 78

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These shards of coalesced necromantic essence are sometimes found in the wake of an ancestor storm. Howling spirits are faintly visible, trapped inside the jagged, dark-green glass.

You can use the shard to cow the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) or briefly release the tormented souls from inside the glass. While you hold the stormshard, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks to [influence](/Rules.aspx?ID=1830) the undead. In addition, you can [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) undead creatures, even if those creatures are [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=652) or otherwise [immune](/Rules.aspx?ID=2313) to [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), or [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects.

**Activate—Free the Spirits** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You briefly release the spirits from the _stormshard_ before drawing them back into the glass. Each creature in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) takes 4d8 [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage (DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2247) Fortitude save). You treat the result of your saving throw as one degree of success better than its outcome.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 6"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Majordomo Torc](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2398)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=280" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 195

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +13; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) vision 30 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) hearing 30 feet

**Communication** speech ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) and 1 imparted language)

**Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +13, [Nobility Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +13, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +13

**Int** +3, **Wis** +3, **Cha** +3

**Will** +14 

</column>

---        

Forged in platinum, a _majordomo torc_ is engraved with heraldic insignias along with one language's alphabet, much like a [_choker of elocution_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=422). You gain a +1 item bonus to [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) checks and the ability to understand, speak, and write the torc's language. Your excellent elocution reduces the DC of the flat check to perform an auditory action while [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) from 5 to 3.

 Upon being invested, the torc appoints itself your majordomo and, given the chance, takes over coordinating your social calendar, engagements, and wardrobe. A _majordomo torc_ has a prim, fussy disposition, and although it defers to you, it can grow sardonic if you frequently ignore its advice. The torc has the following activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _majordomo torc_ casts [_befitting attire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=867) on you, usually to your specifications. However the torc can also choose the appearance of the illusion for you.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Mantle of Far Horizons](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5219)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Dead God's Hand</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 143

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The _mantle of far horizons_ helps to bring comfort and a sense of security while traveling, filling you with confidence and bolstering your energy during long journeys. In areas where you can see the horizon, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) checks made to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=2406).

**Activate—Gaze upon the Horizon** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You raise the mantle's hood to augment your ability to see over large distances or through adverse weather. For the next hour, or until you lower your hood (whichever comes first), you gain a +1 item bonus to Perception checks made to observe things more than 500 feet away, or while in [weather](/Traits.aspx?ID=464)-related conditions that penalize your Perception checks (such as [fog](/Rules.aspx?ID=815) or [precipitation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2816)).

**Activate—Listen to the World** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You lower the mantle's hood to focus on the world's natural sounds rather than other distractions. For the next minute, or until you raise the mantle's hood (whichever comes first), you gain a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) effects.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Astrolabes can be used for navigation in unfamiliar or featureless locations. To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49). An astrolabe also grants a +1 item bonus to checks to identify celestial bodies. A standard astrolabe functions only on steady ground.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mark Of The Torrent](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5252)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 177

**Price** 135 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

**Access** You’re a member of the Order of the Torrent.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The Order of the Torrent works to rescue kidnapped people, and their cobalt blue badge can often open doors that would otherwise be closed. When wearing this badge, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) and [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=2408) or Gather Information about a missing person. 

**Activate—Modus Operandi** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** A kidnapping occurred within 15 feet of your location, or you have some information about the target or perpetrators of a kidnapping; **Effect** You attempt to Recall Knowledge about those who perpetrated the kidnapping, the information supernaturally surfacing in your mind. The GM determines what skill and DC to use for this check based on the level and nature of the perpetrators (usually a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) check at a standard DC for the perpetrator’s level). In addition, if you fail to Recall Knowledge about the kidnapper (but don’t critically fail), you eliminate one false lead about the kidnapper or how they abducted the target. For instance, you might determine that an incorporeal undead wasn’t involved, though you gain no other information about what happened. The mark can’t provide specific identifying information about the perpetrators, like their name or location.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<traits>

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A standard deck of cards consists of 54 cards made from thick paper contained within a paper sleeve. The most common deck used for games and gambling is known as the Old Mage deck and features four suits themed with the four essences of magic, each with 13 cards, as well as two wildcards. The name and appearance of the deck varies from region to region, such as the Magician's Deck in Taldor or the Deck of Masks in the Shackles.

<column gap="tiny">

>
Marked Playing Cards
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 115

**Price** 1 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

</row>

</column>

---

A deck of marked playing cards appears to be an ordinary deck upon initial inspection but bears specific folds, colors, scratches, or other markings on each card that allow an informed user to know what's on the other side of a card. A deck of marked cards grants you a +1 item bonus to [Games Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks or other relevant checks to gamble with the cards. You can determine that an unattended deck of cards is marked with a successful DC 20 Perception check. Determining that a deck is marked during play is more difficult and is typically determined by a Perception check against the dealer's Games Lore or [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC.

**Bulk** 1

<row gap="medium">

---

This short, thick, stick-like object is crafted of wood and steel. Precious metals decorate the grip, and fine filigree marks the caps on each end. A _marshal’s baton_ grants you a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) and [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks against troops, individual soldiers, and military leaders.

**Activate—Stentorian Order** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You issue a command in a booming voice while gesturing with the _marshal’s baton_ and cast a [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1470) spell (DC 18). This spell affects [troops](/Rules.aspx?ID=3364) and [swarms](/Traits.aspx?ID=707) as if they were a single creature.

This [healer's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=25) contains a seemingly endless supply of bandages, herbs, and healing items of impeccable quality, granting you a +2 item bonus to Medicine checks. If you use the _marvelous medicines_ when you [Treat a Poison](/Actions.aspx?ID=56) or [Treat a Disease](/Actions.aspx?ID=55), before you roll your check, the medicines attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the poison or disease you're treating, with a counteract rank of 5 and a counteract modifier of +21. This is a healing effect. The medicines can't be used to treat the same affliction for that patient again.

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 186 **Price** 24,000 gp **Usage** worn mask **Bulk** L --- This mask appears to be a pool of mirrored, shifting silver adhered to a thin metal plate. When you place it against your face, it melds to the shape of your head. The material is breathable and light, and does not obscure vision. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks while wearing the mask. When you invest the mask, you either increase your Charisma score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score. **Activate** envision ([visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You attempt a Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, or Performance check; **Effect** You gain a +4 status bonus to the triggering check. This ability has no effect if you're under the effects of a disguise that hides the _mask of allure_. Depending on the skill used, the mirrored silver transforms into one of the following appearances.
  • **Deception** A swirl of silver, which entirely obscures and conceals your normal features.
  • **Diplomacy** A kind, gentle and inviting expression.
  • **Intimidation** A monstrous visage that shocks viewers into paying attention.
  • **Performance** A jovial humanoid face, the mouth cracked wide with a comedic smile or a tragic frown, depending on the nature of the performance.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 7"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Mask of Shifting Monstrosity](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4005)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane
](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 80

**Price** 360 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This mask’s features shift between various nonhuman elements, with each version reveling in grotesque and monstrous variations. During the festivals in Dhuraxilis, these masks are worn by influential and rich humans (or human-appearing populations) to better blend in with the monstrous crowds as they join in the revelry. While wearing the mask, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks.

**Activate—Monstrosity Meld** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You take on the general appearance of a type of non-humanoid creature that you can see, with the transformation lasting for 8 hours. Activating this effect doesn’t change your traits or statistics, nor does it grant any of the special abilities of the creature you’re imitating. It does not change your size, so a Medium creature that assumes the shape of a manticore remains Medium sized. This effect uses the same rules as the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) activity of [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38). Onlookers always assume you’re the chosen type of creature unless they’re actively Seeking. You gain a +4 item bonus to your Deception DC against such Perception checks and add your level even if untrained.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Mask of the Mantis](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3497)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Prey for Death</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 104

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn head

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The traditional headwear for the Red Mantis assassin is the _mask of the mantis_. Most of these masks are constructed from hard leather helmets that serve to obscure the assassin's identity and give them the appearance of possessing a mantis's head. Some variants, however, consist only of the mask itself, and are meant to be worn over the face. Regardless of the shape and style, all _masks of the mantis_ function the same.

 Members of the Vernai can use any mask of the mantis to enhance their frightening presence—something they often do simply to reveal their standing in the society without speaking a word, as detailed fully in the entry for Vernai's Ire activation below.

 While wearing a _mask of the mantis_, you gain a +1 item bonus to Perception checks.

**Activate—Enhance Vision** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast either [_darkvision_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1481) or [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663) on yourself.

**Activate—Vernai's Ire** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32))   **Requirements** You are a member of the Vernai; **Effect** You cause the mask of the mantis's eyes to shimmer with crimson light, granting yourself a far more harrowing visage. This light creates illumination equivalent to that of a candle. You can use this ability again to extinguish the frightening glow, but as long as Vernai's Ire remains active, you gain a +1 item bonus to Intimidation checks.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 11"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mask of Uncanny Breath](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2326)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Focused" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=74" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 150

**Price** 1,200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A thin wooden mask carved in the shape of a skull, monstrous face, or eerily featureless visage, a mask of uncanny breath fully covers your face. While wearing it, each breath you take feels cool and pure, perfectly flowing to feed your qi. You gain resistance 10 to [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96) [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) and can breathe in an airless or toxic environment. When you breathe in, fragments of bizarre knowledge flow through you, granting you a +2 item bonus to [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to cast an [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) monk qi spell. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** Your [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) Strike hits a creature that breathes;  **Effect** The mask contorts and inhales, sucking breath from your target's lungs. The target falls [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) but doesn't fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) or drop what it's holding. It wakes up at the end of your turn if it hasn't been woken up already.

**Craft Requirements** You are a [monk](/Classes.aspx?ID=8) with occult qi spells.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Craft Requirements** You are a [monk](/Classes.aspx?ID=60) with [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) ki spells.

Elegant jewelry such as the _master magus ring_ adorns experienced [magi](/Classes.aspx?ID=17). You gain a +2 item bonus to [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to cast a magus conflux spell. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The ring transports you and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space you can see within a range equal to your Speed. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) container—the activation fails and is used.

**Craft Requirements** You are a magus.

>
[Mattock of the Titans](/Equipment.aspx?ID=391)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 601

**Price** 36,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 16
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Greatpick](/Weapons.aspx?ID=23)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This 15-foot-long [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374) digging tool is far too big for even a Large creature to wield, though if you’re a Small or larger creature, you can wield it while wearing a [_belt of giant strength_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=398), as though it were appropriately sized for you and had 2 Bulk. The GM might also allow you to wield the mattock if you have some other means of wielding oversized weapons, such as if you’re a Large barbarian with the [giant instinct](/Instincts.aspx?ID=4) or are a Huge creature. When it’s used as a weapon, the _mattock of the titans_ has the statistics of a _+3 greater striking [keen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=300) adamantine [greatpick](/Weapons.aspx?ID=23)_.

 While you’re wielding the _mattock of the titans_, you gain a +3 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks. You can use it to loosen or push soft earth at a rate of 1 minute per 5-foot cube or smash through solid stone at the rate of 5 minutes per 5-foot-cube.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You dig furiously with the mattock to non-magically replicate the effects of an [_earthquake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=95) spell.

**Craft Requirements** You are a titan, and the initial raw materials must include 8,100 gp of adamantine.

[Magical Medals](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3971)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Military leaders or heads of state award these special medals to commend exemplary performance by their top soldiers. They’re typically worn on a special strip of fabric near the lapel, but soldiers from different countries sometimes wear them in other places. No matter how many _magical medals_ you have, they collectively count as one invested item.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 3"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of Gorilla’s Might
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 25 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This steel medal resembles the head and upper body of a [gorilla](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2827). It’s typically given in recognition of physical prowess, and it grants you a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374), [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=2375), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377), and [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378).

**Activate—Gorila's Second Leap** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would fail but not critically fail an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378);  **Effect** The gorilla on the medal beats its chest, giving you another chance. You reroll the failed check.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 4"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of Griffon’s Heart
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 80 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This copper medal features a [griffon’s](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3034) face, wings, and talons in profile. It is given in recognition of remarkable bravery, and it grants you a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598) and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects. While wearing this pendant, you can also cast [_forbidding ward_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1535) as an [innate](/Rules.aspx?ID=2901) cantrip.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 7"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of the Wolf Pack
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 350 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

There are three [wolf’s](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3241) heads engraved on this pewter medal, typically awarded to squads who demonstrate exceptional teamwork. While wearing the _medal of the wolf pack_, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to damage rolls against enemies you are [flanking](/Rules.aspx?ID=2375).

<title
level="2"
right="Item 12"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of Unicorn’s Purity
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 1,700 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The profile of the [unicorn](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=504) on this silver medal has a horn that extends slightly beyond the circular border. This medal is awarded in recognition of true righteousness and exemplary service to a cause.

**Activate—Unicorn’s Grace** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would regain Hit Points from a [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) effect;  **Effect** You regain an additional 4d6 Hit Points.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 16"
pfs="Standard"
>
Medal of Phoenix’s Fire
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 151

**Price** 9,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The [phoenix](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3137) on this gold medal is proud and fierce, and the medal features a border shaped like a flame. This medal is considered the highest honor in many countries and is awarded to those soldiers who have truly exemplified the ethics of their country through unbelievable service.

**Activate—Phoenix’s Sacrifice** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** Your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition increases;  **Effect** The phoenix bursts into flames. You lose the dying condition and regain 1 Hit Point. Your [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=99) value does not increase. You can use this action while [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95).

This [standard-grade dawnsilver shield](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2814) (Hardness 5, HP 20, BT 10) is inscribed with the symbol of a deity dedicated to [healing](/Domains.aspx?ID=78) and medicine. The shield is designed for combat medics to aid combatants or adventurers in the midst of battle. [Healer’s tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2727) can be stored on the backside of this shield. This shield grants a +2 item bonus to [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) checks.

**Activate—Adrenaline Boost** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You grant a medicinal boost to bring someone back into the fray. You [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396) to stabilize an adjacent ally with the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition. On a success, they gain 6d6+20 Hit Points, can immediately [Stand](/Actions.aspx?ID=2303) as a free action, and become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for 1 round. They can use this extra action only to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) or [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306).

**Price** 20 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

The time-honored tradition of weaving beautiful, embroidered glory ribbons throughout one’s hair and beard remains an important cultural practice among some dwarven clans, with the choice of colors and style of presentation representing status, achievements, and other significant aspects of someone’s position. Magical versions also exist that help enhance the wearer’s memory. These magical ribbons are especially popular when someone has been invited to serve as a toastmaster at a guild banquet or as a master of ceremonies at an important festival. Their use in final oral exams for high positions is, however, hotly debated.

**Activate—Read the Ribbon's Story** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** You attempt a skill check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) but haven’t rolled yet;  **Effect** The _memory ribbon_ grants you a +2 item bonus to the triggering skill check to Recall Knowledge. Afterward, the ribbon becomes non-magical.

---

This hot, broth-based soup typically contains tubers, leeks, zesty spices, reagents, and if desired, the meat of livestock. Civic authorities commission batches of mender's soup for workers if a tricky job is on the agenda. After you eat the soup, its effects last 24 hours or until you make your next daily preparations, whichever comes first. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks to [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=42) and restore an additional 5 Hit Points to items you successfully Repair during this time. 

If you eat mender's soup over the entire period required to attempt a Crafting check to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) (typically a minimum of eating the soup each day for 4 days), the +1 bonus from the soup can be applied to that check, too.

fields.text: Item 2 Mender's Soup Alchemical Consumable Processed Source Treasure Vault pg. 49 Price 5 gp Usage held in 2 hands Bulk L Activate 10 minutes (Interact) This hot, broth-based soup typically contains tubers, leeks, zesty spices, reagents, and if desired, the meat of livestock. Civic authorities commission batches of mender’s soup for workers if a tricky job is on the agenda. After you eat the soup, its effects last 24 hours or until you make your next daily preparations, whichever comes first. You gain a +1 item bonus to Crafting checks to Repair and restore an additional 5 Hit Points to items you successfully Repair during this time. If you eat mender’s soup over the entire period required to attempt a Crafting check to Craft (typically a minimum of eating the soup each day for 4 days), the +1 bonus from the soup can be applied to that check, too.

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 187 **Price** 24,000 gp **Usage** worn cloak **Bulk** L --- This deep red cloak fits lightly about your shoulders, and the edges perpetually twitch slightly, as though caught in a breeze. The cloth feels smoother than silk, rippling and swaying like liquid when in motion. You feel a lively energy infusing your arms and legs. You gain a +3 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) and [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15), and a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against attacks from reactions triggered by your movement. When you invest the cloak, you either increase your Dexterity score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score. **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** An enemy misses you with a melee Strike; **Effect** You slip around the attacking creature with ease. You Step, without moving away from the triggering enemy, and then make a melee Strike against the triggering enemy if it's within reach. If you do make a Strike, the target attempts a DC 38 Perception check before you roll. **Failure** This creature is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) against the Strike.
**Critical Failure** This creature is flat-footed against all your attacks until the end of their next turn. **Activate** command, envision ([conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The cloak hums with power as your whirl it around yourself, disappearing amid a brief flash of light. Teleport up to double your Speed to a location you can see. At the end of the teleportation, you can make a melee Strike against a creature within reach, if there is one.

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 292

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

This silver signet ring changes to match the insignia of a leader or organization you serve (or your own face, if you serve no one else). It grants you a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks and lets you cast [_message_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1598) as an arcane innate spell at will. 

**Activate—Dispatch Messenger** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The ring casts [_animal messenger_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1441) to your specification. The animal is a magical creature that springs from the ring, and its appearance suits the iconography or heraldry of the leader or organization represented by the ring.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 11"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mind's Light Circlet](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2328)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Focused" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=74" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=100" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 150

**Price** 1,200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Gemstones of many colors adorn the silver of a _mind's light circlet_. When you're charged with mental power, the jewels scintillate with light, with different gems resonating based on your emotions. If you have at least 1 Focus Point, the gems cast [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) in a 10-foot radius. When you amp a spell, the light increases to [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 20-foot radius (and dim light to the next 20 feet) until the start of your next turn.

 You gain a +2 item bonus to [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) checks. You also gain the following [amp](/Traits.aspx?ID=425), which you can apply to any of your psi cantrips that have a target or area, much like an amp gained from a feat.

 **Amp** You transfer some of the magical luminescence from the mind's light circlet to one of the creatures. Choose a creature targeted by the spell or in its area. Until the start of your next turn, that creature sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light to the next 20 feet) and can't be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4). If the creature is [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), it's concealed while alight, rather than being [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39).

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to use a psychic amp. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

**Craft Requirements** You are a [psychic](/Classes.aspx?ID=21).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These goggles feature highly reflective lenses. While wearing the goggles, you gain a +1 item bonus to visual Perception checks and to saving throws against [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) effects.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))  **Trigger** A creature within 60 feet targets you with a visual effect;  **Effect** You turn your head to reflect aspects of the triggering effect back at its creator. The creature must attempt a DC 20 Fortitude save as it becomes disoriented by this reflection. On a failure, the creature is [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34) (sickened 2 on a critical failure). The creature is temporarily immune for 1 hour.

>
[Mnemonic Feather](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3523)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 43

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Murrou crafted these feathers to assist in remembering information. A _mnemonic feather_ is an emu feather imbued with magical energies. You can place the _mnemonic feather_ in a book with an Interact action. As long as the _mnemonic feather_ remains within the book, you recall information contained within that book perfectly, as if you were reading the page, as long as the book is on the same plane as you. When you attempt to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about a topic contained within the book, you gain a +1 status bonus to the check. 

**Activate—Recite Mnemonic** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** An ally within 30 feet attempts a [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) check involving the topic in the _mnemonic feather’s_ book;  **Effect** You mentally impart the book’s knowledge to your ally, giving them the benefit of the _mnemonic feather_.

<title

    right="Item 13"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Mocker's Swazzle](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3630)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Curtain Call</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 80

**Price** 3,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A swazzle is a device made of two strips of metal bound with sinew and around a reed that, when held to the mouth, causes the user’s voice to take on a distinctive rasping tone. Swazzles are often used by street puppeteers to give their puppets’ voices a unique and memorable timber. A _mocker’s swazzle_, though, has a different use—rather than simply giving voices to troublemaking puppets, it helps a performer fight back against hecklers in a crowd.

**Activate—Heckle the Heckler** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** A creature within 30 feet of you attempts and fails to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) you;  **Effect** You quickly fire a retort back at the triggering creature, mocking its failed attempt in a way that makes it laugh at its own ineptitude; you cast [_laughing fit_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1583) (DC 30 Will save) on the triggering creature. 

**Activate—Mocking Spell** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=642), [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You direct a quick bit of insulting mockery at a creature who can understand you that’s within earshot. If your next action is to cast a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) spell that targets only that creature, that creature takes a –1 item penalty to any saving throw against the spell and, regardless of the result of the saving throw, becomes [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of your next turn.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 78

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Pathfinder Society does not use vehicle rules_

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** You're from the Mordant Spire

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The swirls on this wooden mask—often worn by Mordant Censors—move and shift, reflecting the shape of the nearest currents. Wearing the mask grants you a +1 item bonus to [Sailing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) and [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) checks. In addition, it allows you to pilot a boat with simply a thought. When you pilot a vehicle, you can keep both hands free and [Drive](/Actions.aspx?ID=3517) from any location on the vehicle. 

**Activate—Set the Course** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You are aboard a vehicle; **Effect** You become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for 1 minute or until you leave the vehicle, whichever comes first, and can use the extra action to [Take Control](/Actions.aspx?ID=3520) of the vehicle or, if you’re already piloting it, Drive or [Stop](/Actions.aspx?ID=3519) the vehicle.

<traits>

This small brass pin is shaped like a monkey climbing a tree. When you activate this talisman, use a [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33) action with a +1 item bonus on the check. On this check and until the end of your turn, if you succeed on an Athletics check to Climb, you move your full Speed during the Climb. If you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />

**Bulk** L

---

This delicate and elegant diadem is woven of intricate silver wires set with three tear-shaped pearlescent moonstones. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> focus;  **Frequency** once per hour;  **Requirements** You are within 10 feet of a _moonstone pool_; **Effect** You peer into the _moonstone pool_ and gain access to all the visual history recorded within the receptacle by concentrating on the specific subject you wish to see. Conversely, you can choose to deposit your own memories into the pool by concentrating for 1 hour on the information you wish to impart.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Motion-Seeking Lenses](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3973)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 152

**Price** 55 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When you wear these green-tinted glasses, all the movement in the surrounding area seems to jump out at you. You gain a +1 item bonus to your [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=3303) DC against [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) checks to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) or [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405), and anyone attempting to Sneak doesn’t benefit from the circumstance bonus from [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372) against your Perception DC.

**Activate—Find the Hidden** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([detection](/Traits.aspx?ID=574), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You twist the lenses of your glasses as you look for someone hidden. You [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) with a +1 item bonus. If you find a [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) creature or object, you can [Point Out](/Actions.aspx?ID=2315) as a free action.

</column>

Handheld instruments include bagpipes, a small set of chimes, small drums, fiddles and viols, flutes and recorders, small harps, lutes, trumpets, and similarly sized instruments. The GM might rule that an especially large handheld instrument (like a tuba) has greater Bulk. >
[Needle of Undeath](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3687)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Triumph of the Tusk</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #209: Destroyer's Doom](/Sources.aspx?ID=251) pg. 83

**Price** 1,150 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This thin, wand-like implement is carved from bone and scrimshawed with depictions of battle. While holding the needle of undeath, [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=652) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) creatures see you as one of their own and are [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=82) to you until you take [hostile actions](/Rules.aspx?ID=2251) against them, and you have a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) and [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks against intelligent undead. This does not affect a summoned undead’s attitude.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Speak with Undead;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You can use Diplomacy to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) on mindless undead or make simple requests of them with a +2 item bonus. You cannot make this request of someone else’s summoned undead.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    right="Item 12+"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Nosoi Charm](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1095)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Night of the Gray Death</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Night of the Gray Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=99) pg. 53

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Nosois serve as scribes and messengers to psychopomps. They are rare outside of the Boneyard, so it's common for [psychopomps](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83) venturing to other planes to carry a nosoi facsimile to aid in their travels. This tiny icon of a masked raven emits twittering sounds in perfect accompaniment to your performances. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks to play an instrument, orate, or sing. You can cast [_sending_](/Spells.aspx?ID=272) once per day as a divine innate spell. 

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You twist the base of the charm, and the twittering it emits becomes helpful words to boost your arguments. You lose the item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks and gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to make [Requests](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) until you use this activation again.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You gain [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=21) as an imprecise sense with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour as long as you continue to hold the charm. This allows you to sense the life force that animates living creatures and the perverse force that animates the dead, though you can't distinguish between the two.

</title>

<traits>

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Nosois serve as scribes and messengers to psychopomps. They are rare outside of the Boneyard, so it's common for [psychopomps](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83) venturing to other planes to carry a nosoi facsimile to aid in their travels. This tiny icon of a masked raven emits twittering sounds in perfect accompaniment to your performances. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks to play an instrument, orate, or sing. You can cast [_sending_](/Spells.aspx?ID=272) once per day as a divine innate spell. 

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You twist the base of the charm, and the twittering it emits becomes helpful words to boost your arguments. You lose the item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks and gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to make [Requests](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) until you use this activation again.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You gain [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=21) as an imprecise sense with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour as long as you continue to hold the charm. This allows you to sense the life force that animates living creatures and the perverse force that animates the dead, though you can't distinguish between the two.

>
[Oathlamp of Accord](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3575)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=640" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 103

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This hooded lantern takes the form of a translucent prism. It functions as a normal [hooded lantern](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2730), except that it isn’t fueled by oil, but by oaths. While you’re holding the lantern, you gain a +1 item bonus to Diplomacy checks.

**Activate—Annouce Oath** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647))  **Trigger** You make a promise in good faith;  **Effect** The _oathlamp of accord_ sheds light without consuming fuel until the promise you made is broken or fulfilled. The GM adjudicates whether a spoken promise is broken or fulfilled. This light and the shutters to conceal it work as normal for a hooded lantern. Any creature in the light of the oathlamp becomes aware of the contents of the oath, along with who made it and how long ago.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 15"
    pfs=""
>
[Oculus of Abaddon](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1747)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Evil" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=64" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 587

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

An _oculus of Abaddon_ is a potent artifact rumored to have been created by one of the [Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=11) as a way to reward those who work as their agents on the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1). More likely, these items were crafted by a powerful pre-Earthfall death cult that has long since moved on, leaving behind these dangerous artifacts to tempt mortals into serving the needs of the Horsemen. 

An _oculus of Abaddon_ appears as a sphere of clear crystal that contains a pinpoint of flickering red light at its center. When held, the oculus feels warm to the touch and fills you with a sudden desire to pluck out an eye and place the oculus within the socket—this causes 4d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). Once placed in an eye socket, the oculus can be removed only by ripping it free (causing the same amount of persistent bleed damage as the initial plucking). When you place the oculus in your empty eye socket, you immediately heal all damage caused by plucking the previous eye out. Once placed, an oculus grants you constant [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415). It can also be activated to perform a number of other magical effects, as detailed below, but if you aren't evil, each time you activate an _oculus of Abaddon_, you must succeed at a DC 36 Will save or become affected by a [_subconscious suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=314) (heightened to 8th level) to perform an evil act the next time an opportunity to do so arises, as determined by the GM.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (envision);  **Frequency** three times per day;   **Effect** You gain the effects of [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=268), heightened to 7th level.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** You use the _oculus of Abaddon_ to cast a [_planar binding_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=17) ritual, heightened to 7th level. You can only conjure neutral evil creatures with this casting of _planar binding_. If you already know the _planar binding_ ritual, you gain a +3 item bonus on the primary check when casting _planar binding_.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> envision;    **Requirements** you have a [familiar](/Rules.aspx?ID=160) or [animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=149); **Effect** You can see and hear through your familiar or animal companion's eyes and ears, provided you are on the same plane. This effect can be sustained, but as long as you do so you can take no other actions.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 hour (envision; [evil](/Traits.aspx?ID=64)) **Frequency** once per year;   **Effect** You manipulate the minds of a huge number of targets, provided that the end goal of the manipulation is a tragic or otherwise horrific fate for those being manipulated. This functions as [_suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=315), but with a range of 1 mile. All creatures within this area are affected, with the same suggestion implanted in their minds. Creatures hear the telepathic suggestion in their native language, and creatures that are 7th level or higher can attempt a DC 36 Will save to resist the effect. This power was used by Vordakai to cause the vanishing of Varnhold, suggesting to its inhabitants to leave their homes and travel south to his tomb. If this effect is [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) or removed on one victim, it ends for all victims.

**Destruction** A foul and hideous object, an _oculus of Abaddon_ is fortunately relatively easy to destroy, as far as artifacts go. It has Hardness 25 and 100 Hit Points, but repairs damage to itself swiftly, regaining 10 Hit Points per round. It has weakness 10 to bludgeoning damage and weakness 30 to good damage.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Your eyes bulge from their sockets and extend upwards from your head on long, prehensile stalks, greatly enhancing your eyesight and field of view but leaving you unable to close your eyes, increasing your vulnerability to harmful visual effects.

**Benefit** You gain [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49), a +2 item bonus to visual [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2298) checks, and [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=2411) if you don’t already have it. These effects last for 1 minute.

**Drawback** For 1 minute, you take a –2 penalty to saving throws against effects that have the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 121

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

One hundred cuts, healed into diamond-shaped scars, represent the ability to withstand the attacks of your enemies. [Orc](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=19) warriors covet these scar patterns and cluster them around what they consider to be their strongest assets—a pattern around the heart signifies a warrior with great endurance, while one along the arms indicates great upper body strength. 

You gain a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks. If you have [Ferocity](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=16) (such as from the [Orc Ferocity](/Feats.aspx?ID=83) feat or a similar ability), the first time each day you use it, instead of remaining at 1 Hit Point, your Hit Points are set to an amount equal to your ancestry Hit Points, even if this amount is more than you had before using Ferocity.

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 64

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=41)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This [leather armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=41) has been treated with extract from [oozes](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=453), which can be reactivated in the presence of a strong acid. A receptacle in the armor can hold an [acid flask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3286), which takes 3 Interact actions to install.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** An acid flask is installed in the armor; **Effect** The leather weeps slippery protoplasm, granting an item bonus to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) and [Squeeze](/Actions.aspx?ID=2372) checks equal to the acid flask’s item bonus. </title>

<traits>

<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 151

**Price** 1,200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Patterns themed to your curse cover your _oracular crown_. As your curse worsens, the appearance of the crown changes, introducing extreme angles, stronger colors, or other indications of the intensity of your curse. Similarly, it gets closer to its natural form when you reduce the effects of your curse. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can use only to cast an oracle revelation spell. If not used by the end of your turn, this Focus Point is lost.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** Your [cursebound](/Traits.aspx?ID=800) value is 1 or higher; **Effect** You regain 3d8 Hit Points. The amount of healing increases to 5d8 if you’re cursebound 2, 7d8 if you’re cursebound 3, or 9d8 if you’re cursebound 4. If you have the [void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83) ability, this activation has the [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) trait instead of the healing and vitality traits.

**Craft Requirements** You are an [oracle](/Classes.aspx?ID=14).

---

Granted by Katapesh's Pactmasters to influential merchants, exceptional [Zephyr Guards](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=35), and favorite retainers, a _pactmaster's grace_ is a crystal-studded blue platinum ring that sharpens the wearer's urban instincts. While invested, the ring grants a +2 item bonus to saving throws while you are in an urban setting, and this increases to a +3 item bonus if you have legendary proficiency in Guild [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8), Katapesh Lore, Mercantile Lore, or [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14). You also gain a +3 item bonus to Mercantile Lore checks while wearing the ring, and you can attempt checks that require a proficiency rank of master in Society.

---

Parade armor is an armor adjustment that creates a set of pseudo-decorative armor to wear during noncombat functions. Any medium or heavy armor can be fashioned into parade armor, which features custom designs based on the wearer's affiliation, military branch, or rank. A particular faction typically has one uniform appearance for its set of parade armor. While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) and [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks against creatures of the same affiliation as your parade armor, though the bonus to Intimidation doesn't apply when interacting with creatures of higher rank than you. The armor is slightly bulkier, increasing the Bulk by 1.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 127 _[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The standard version is permitted for use while the greater and major versions are limited._ **Usage** affixed to armor or a weapon --- This ornate doorknob can open doors both material and metaphysical, revealing dreams and nightmares. The spell DC of any spell cast by activating this item is 20.
  • **Armor** You gain a +1 item bonus to [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) checks to [Pick a Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=70).
  • **Weapon** If you critically succeed at a Strike with the weapon, the target is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) until the end of its next turn.
**Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You cast [_figment_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1528). Phantasmal Doorknob **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 127 **Price** 215 gp --- **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast [_phantasmal treasure_](/Spells.aspx?ID=707). Phantasmal Doorknob (Greater) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 127 **Price** 900 gp --- The item bonus when affixed to armor is +2, and the spell DC is 27. On a critical hit with a weapon the doorknob is affixed to, the target is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) until the end of its next turn. The creature is then temporarily immune to being blinded this way for 24 hours. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast [_vision of death_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1742). Phantasmal Doorknob (Major) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 127 **Price** 6,000 gp --- The item bonus when affixed to armor is +2, and the spell DC is 34. On a critical hit with a weapon the doorknob is affixed to, the target is blinded until the end of its next turn. The creature is then temporarily immune to being blinded this way for 24 hours. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast 6th-rank _vision of death_. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast [_phantasmal calamity_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1630).

    level="1"

    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Phantom Piano](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2400)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Focused" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=74" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=280" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 196

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** 2 hands

**Bulk** 16
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +22; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) vision 30 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) hearing 30 feet

**Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) (any languages the possessing spirit knew in life)

**Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +23, [Music Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +23, [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) +25, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +21

**Int** +3, **Wis** +4, **Cha** +5

**Will** +22 

</column>

---        

When a skilled musician dies before reaching their full potential or accomplishing an important goal, their soul might refuse to move on to the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=15). Rather than becoming [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), the spirit possesses an instrument they played in life, turning it into an intelligent item and a [virtuoso instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37). (Other _phantom instruments_ exist, but most are heavy.) A _phantom piano_ offers a bargain to any bard or other skilled musician who finds it: receive musical aid as you dedicate yourself to reaching the success the spirit felt they were denied in life. The piano refuses to play for those who reject this deal. If you accept, the piano asks only that you practice with it and perform for increasingly refined and august audiences, requiring a successful [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check appropriate to your proficiency level. The piano sets no strict timeline, but at the GM's discretion, if you go too long without making progress, the piano can cease cooperating with you until it's satisfied with your dedication once again.

 While you keep up your end of the bargain, the piano grants you a +2 item bonus to Performance checks made with it. The piano also provides access to composition spells based on your Performance proficiency rank, as if you had the corresponding feat. The spells you can use comprise a cumulative list, but you can cast them only when using the piano. You must spend the actions and Focus Points required to cast these spells.

**Trained**  [_courageous anthem_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1763), [_uplifting overture_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1779)

**Expert**  [hymn of healing](/Feats.aspx?ID=4574), [_rallying anthem_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1773)

**Master**  [_symphony of the unfettered heart_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1777)

**Legendary**  [_soothing ballad_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1776)

 A _phantom piano_ has the following activations.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** The piano shrinks down to a figurine of light Bulk compact enough to store in a pouch, or from figurine form back to instrument form. In figurine form, the piano doesn't function as an instrument or provide magic other than this activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to Cast a Spell the piano provides you.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

A phantom roll contains vegetables, greens, and fine, clear noodles, all wrapped in transparent, edible starch paper and alchemically treated and laced with a tangy sauce. Upon eating the roll, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks you attempt during the [Avoid Notice](/Actions.aspx?ID=511) exploration activity. You can also Avoid Notice at full Speed or combine it with [Investigate](/Actions.aspx?ID=516) or [Scout](/Actions.aspx?ID=518) while moving at half Speed. These effects expire 24 hours after you eat the roll or when you make your next daily preparations, whichever comes first.

Upon eating the roll, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) checks you attempt during the [Avoid Notice](/Actions.aspx?ID=2622) exploration activity. You can also Avoid Notice at full Speed or combine it with [Investigate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2627) or Scout while moving at half Speed. These effects expire 24 hours after you eat the roll or when you make your next [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), whichever comes first.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 25"
    pfs=""
>
[Philosopher's Extractor](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3122)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 301

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 8
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This bizarre machine is a complex arrangement of flasks, tubes, and other alchemical equipment. The _philosopher's extractor_ is designed to create the ultimate alchemical concoctions. The extractor functions as an [exceptional alchemist's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2702), granting a +4 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks related to alchemy.  When using the extractor to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) an alchemical item or with [infused reagents](/Classes.aspx?ID=1) as part of your daily preparations, you can create impeccable alchemical items. An impeccable alchemical item always uses the maximum numerical value possible for any rolls it requires, such as dealing maximum damage with [alchemist's fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=75) or restoring the maximum number of Hit Points with an [elixir of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=91). If the impeccable item has a duration, it lasts twice as long as normal. Finally, an impeccable alchemical item never has a drawback.

**Activate—Accelerated Synthesis** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You use the extractor to produce an alchemical item of your level or lower whose formula you know. The extractor can create 56 levels' worth of items per day in this way. For example, the extractor could create two true elixirs of life (19th level) and two moderate elixirs of life (9th level), or eight [comprehension elixirs](/Equipment.aspx?ID=88) (7th level), and so on.

**Activate—Essence Transmogrification** <actions string="" /> 1 hour (manipulate)    **Effect** You take a sizable portion of a creature (at least two-thirds of its original mass) and filter it through the mechanisms of the extractor. After the end of the process, the _philosopher's extractor_ creates a transmogrifying mutagen that imparts the essence of the creature to the drinker. The extractor can make several transmogrifying mutagens simultaneously using the same activation if enough mass is provided at once, up to a maximum of 10 concurrent mutagens. Drinking a transmogrifying mutagen imparts you with one of the creature's unique abilities for 1 hour. This could grant one of several abilities such as a dragon's breath, [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), flight, [frightful presence](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=17), or immunity to [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145). The ability functions as it did for the original creature, except it uses your class DC or your spell DC (whichever is higher) instead of the creature's DC. The mutagen grants only abilities based on a creature's physiology and never grants magic-related abilities such as innate spells or spellcasting ability. The GM ultimately decides what ability a transmogrifying mutagen grants.

 Unlike normal for [mutagens](/Traits.aspx?ID=116) and [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127) effects, you can drink multiple transmogrifying mutagens and gain benefits from each. When you drink transmogrifying mutagens made from different creatures, you receive abilities from each creature. When you drink multiple transmogrifying mutagens made from the same type of creature, such as multiple mutagens made from trolls, you gain an additional ability for each transmogrifying mutagen you drink, and the duration of the abilities from that creature type increases by 1 hour for each additional concoction you drink.

 However, these additional benefits come with a risk; if you drink a transmogrifying mutagen while at least one other is active, after drinking it, you must succeed at a flat check with a DC equal to the total number of active transmogrifying mutagens you've consumed. On a failure, you fully transform into a member of the species of the latest transmogrifying mutagen you drank, and you almost always go berserk from your change. The transformation may leave some amount of your personality and memories intact, at the GM's discretion.

**Destruction** Simultaneously feeding the _philosopher's extractor_ sizable portions of an [aeon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=2), [angel](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=3), [archon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=9), [azata](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=10), [daemon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=26), [demon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=28), [devil](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30), [protean](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=82), and [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83), each of at least 14th level, along with a [philosopher's stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=133) causes the device to jam, overheat, and explode. Creatures within 60 feet of the explosion must succeed at a DC 55 Reflex save or become covered in an alchemical slurry that transforms them into a horrifying amalgam of at least two of the creatures used to destroy the machine.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

This tiny box holds a fragment of religious scripture sacred to a particular deity. The box is worn by affixing it to a leather cord and tying it around your head just above your brow. You don’t gain any benefit from the phylactery if you don’t worship the affiliated deity. The phylactery grants you religious wisdom, which manifests as a +2 item bonus to Religion checks. Just before you perform an action that would be anathema to the phylactery’s deity, the phylactery warns you of the potential transgression in time for you to change your mind.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You ask for guidance about a particular course of action, gaining the effects of an [_augury_](/Spells.aspx?ID=15) spell.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Pickpocket's Tailoring](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1320)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 50

**Price** 100 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** sewn into clothing

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Pickpocket's tailoring modifies an existing outfit by adding concealed interior pockets and strategically opened seams for hiding small objects inside the lining. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks to [Conceal an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=61) of light Bulk or less in the pockets. When you get a failure (but not a critical failure, which works as normal) on a Stealth check to Conceal such an Object, observers know you're concealing an object somewhere, but they don't find the object unless they succeed at a DC 20 Perception check to locate the seams in the garment.

    level="1"
    right="Item 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Pilferer's Gloves](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2141)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 104

**Price** 15,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn gloves

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Made of soft and subtle black leather, these gloves fit tightly but aren't uncomfortable and don't impede your sense of touch. As long as you're trained in [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) while wearing these gloves, you're always considered one skill rank higher than your actual rank. If you possess a Legendary skill rank in Thievery, you gain a +2 item bonus to Thievery checks instead. When you invest the gloves, you either increase your Dexterity modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You fail or critically fail a Thievery skill check;  **Effect** If you failed the Thievery skill check, you succeed at that check instead. If you critically failed, you fail instead.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
